title: `ward status` and `ward doctor`: safe state and read-only health reporting
description: Spec section 8's command table lists two commands that no WCLI task owned: 'ward status --json' (safe current-project and backend state; no global inventory or secret previews) and 'ward doctor --json' (read-only permissions, key-provider, schema, binding and instruction health; never dump keys or request headers). Filed at opum-agent's ruling (2026-09-28) after WCLI-7's session surfaced the gap, as one task because both are read-only reporting over the same project/binding/vault state. Scope: both commands and their contract tests. Non-goals: profile readiness reporting is 'ward check' (WCLI-9); operational events are 'ward audit' (WCLI-11).

acceptanceCriteria.text: Both commands are registered in the CLI contract (help and manifest) and emit the {schemaVersion, kind, data} envelope when passed --json; the contract test enumerates them

`ward status --json` reports the current project state — manifest/binding presence and project id, vault presence, key-provider reachability, schema version — and nothing outside the current project: no alias list, no secret name, value, length or fingerprint, no other project records; asserted by tests over a store seeded with sentinel values in this and another project (T09/T11 discipline)

`ward doctor --json` runs each check read-only — permissions, key-provider, schema, binding, instruction/bridge health — reports per-check results with stable safe codes, exits 0 when every check passes and 6 when any check fails while the others still report; a simulated single-check failure is asserted for each check

Neither command mutates state (vault, keychain, manifest and bridge files byte-identical before and after) and neither emits key material or request headers, asserted by sentinel and before/after byte-comparison tests

plan: 2. Ports: expose the vault record format version through VaultHeader; let a command set its own exit code in CommandOutput.
3. Domain: managedBlockStatus (absent/current/stale) beside upsertManagedBlock, sharing the marker grammar so doctor cannot drift from what init writes.

4. Application: status and doctor over the checkout, ProjectFiles, VaultStore and KeyProvider ports; five read-only doctor checks (permissions, key provider, schema, binding, instructions) with stable codes, every check always reported.
5. Exit semantics: absence is never a failure; a check fails only when its subject is present and wrong or unevaluable; doctor exits 6 iff any check failed.
6. CLI: manifest entries with kinds status.report and doctor.report, composition-root wiring, human text renderers.

7. Tests: each doctor check failed singly with the others still reporting; sentinel no-inventory and no-key-material assertions; before/after byte comparison for no mutation; non-worktree exit 3; contract enumeration extended.
8. ADR 0007 recording the report shape, codes and exit semantics; lore sync, lore check --strict exit 0.
9. bun run check green, independent review over the diff, findings fixed, criteria checked with evidence on the branch, PR into dev, promote dev to main.
implementationNotes: INDEPENDENT REVIEW (2026-09-29, opum-workflow:reviewer over origin/dev..09322c7, dispatched after PR #36 opened). VERDICT: no high-severity defect — no leak, no wrong exit code, no mutation — measured against a real locked vault rather than a stub, with every "could not read" state reported as a failure. FOUR MEDIUM, all disposed in a487cc6: (1) the no-mutation test compared only CLAUDE.md, so a write through the codex path was invisible (its mutant left all 360 tests green) — both bridge files and both directory listings are now compared; (2) the sentinel test never captured the project this checkout is actually bound to, the one id a conflict must withhold (a mutant emitting it passed) — it is now asserted absent from both commands, JSON and text; (3) the binding check reported a manifest that exists but cannot be judged as skipped, where ADR 0007 defines skipped as an absence only — it now fails with the manifest's own code, the same way the schema check already did, and no exit code moves because schema already failed those states; (4) the vault-level unevaluable states were unpinned — mapping vault_store_failed to absent, and a locked vault reporting clean, both passed. A real SQLite lock (BEGIN EXCLUSIVE) and a port-level failing store now pin busy and unreadable, each with its reject/accept pair measured. TWO LOW: the hanging-store test did not assert the exit-explicitly flag, so dropping it was invisible (now asserted; its mutant reddens it); and an empty ward.db reads as absent, by the store's own contract (ADR 0001) — recovery is intact because create accepts that file, and the point is now recorded in ADR 0007 rather than left to be misread as "nothing is on disk". THREE INFORMATIONAL: ok:true on a machine with nothing set up is by design and is now stated in the ADR (ok means no check failed, not that anything is set up); vault.formatVersion in status is the sealed record's version, not the decrypted state document's, which is a separate gate (state_unsupported) — an intentional reading, recorded here; and SQLite's mandatory open-time hot-journal recovery (ADR 0001) is the one inherited exception to "changes nothing", now named in the ADR instead of overclaimed. THE FOUR PREVIOUSLY-INVISIBLE MUTANTS RE-RUN HERE AND EACH NOW REDDENS EXACTLY THE TEST THAT NAMES ITS PROTECTION: bound-id leak 1 of 14 (conflict test); store_failed to absent 1 of 14 (store-failure test); abandonedCall dropped 1 of 14 (hang test); codex write 1 of 14 (byte-comparison test, refined to a write the report itself cannot see). WHAT THE REVIEW DID NOT CHECK, stated by it: the packaged binary (it ran the source entry point; the packaged form was measured separately in this session — exit 0 fresh, exit 6 with a stale block, exit 3 outside a worktree), the secret half of criterion 2 because the vault holds no aliases or secret records yet (WCLI-8+; the test file and ADR 0007 both say so), a hot journal it did not create, and a byte-level listing of sidecars. EVIDENCE AFTER THE FIXES: 362 tests / 0 fail (two new); bun run check green; lore validate --strict and lore check --strict exit 0.
finalSummary: Landed on feat/WCLI-26-status-doctor, PR opum-ai/ward-cli#36; the review-fix commit a487cc6 has CI run 36505593639 green (Check, Docs, Tracker integrity). WHAT: ward status --json reports this checkout's state and nothing outside it - the canonical root, the manifest's claim (project id and schema version), the binding state for this root, the vault's presence, revision and record format version, and the key provider's verdict. A checkout bound to another project is reported as a conflict and that project is never named; a missing key is a reportable condition rather than a refusal, because the vault header is readable without it. ward doctor --json runs five read-only checks in a fixed order (permissions, key_provider, schema, binding, instructions), each with a stable code, always reporting all five; a check fails only when its subject is present and wrong or present and unevaluable, absence is skipped and never fails, and doctor exits 6 when any check failed, with the report on stdout either way. The module is read-only by construction - header, load, read and project file reads only - and renders no key material. ADR 0007 records the report shape, the codes and the exit contract. Port changes: the vault header now carries the sealed record's format version, and a command result may carry its own exit code. VERIFIED: the criteria against tests as evidence, not code presence. The contract test enumerates both commands and their kinds; test/reporting.test.ts (14 cases) covers the status report over a vault seeded with a second project and a second binding (every sentinel absent including the bound project's own id, the current claim present as positive control), the byte-comparison no-mutation case over the vault database, the manifest and both bridge files plus both directory listings, each doctor check failed singly with the others still reporting (insecure permissions, missing and hanging key, a locked vault through a real SQLite lock, a failing store port, a newer manifest, a future state document, unregistered and conflicting bindings, stale and malformed blocks, and the absent-block pass), and exit 3 outside a Git worktree. The packaged binary was measured directly: exit 0 fresh, exit 6 with a stale instruction block, exit 3 outside a worktree. An independent opum-workflow:reviewer pass returned no high-severity defect and four medium, two low and three informational findings, all applied in a487cc6; the four mutants that previously left every test green now each redden exactly the test that names the protection they bypass (the bound project's id emitted in the report; vault_store_failed reported as absent; the exit-explicitly flag dropped; a write through the codex bridge path), and ADR 0007 was corrected where the review showed it overclaimed. 362 tests / 0 fail; bun run check green; lore validate --strict, lore check --strict and lore agents --check exit 0. NOT CHECKED, stated rather than implied: the secret half of the status no-inventory claim, because the vault holds no aliases or secret records yet (WCLI-8+; the sentinel machinery is in place and the test file says so); request headers, because no transport exists in this build (WCLI-10 must re-measure that claim); a hot journal created deliberately; and a byte-level listing of the vault directory's sidecars.
